Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back.The Afghanistan players are out in the middle. Fazalhaq Farooqi to bowl first. George Munsey and Michael Jones to open for Scotland. Let's play...
...The Chase...

A massive task ahead for Scotland - With wickets in hand, Afghanistan floored the accelerator. Nabi joined forces with Rasooli and the gears shifted instantly, the scoring rate climbing without warning. The pair tore into the attack in overdrive, pushing Scotland firmly onto the back foot, before Darwish Rasooli eventually walked off retired out on 84, having done more than enough to tilt the momentum Afghanistan’s way. Runs on the board is always a positive and it will take quite an effort from a spirited Scottish batting unit to scale this down. Back in a bit with the run chase. Stay tuned.

The counterattack through Rasooli and Nabi - Rasooli was the standout, batting with quiet authority and rolling into a brisk half century without any fuss. Scotland were far from poor with the ball. They kept things tight and rarely let Afghanistan run away with the game. What they missed, though, was the killer blow. Whether it was a lack of experience or the pitch not being as flat as it first looked, the wickets never came in a cluster. Between overs 7-15, Afghanistan quietly cashed in, adding 81 runs and setting themselves up for a strong finish before Rasooli and Nabi took the charge for a big finish.

Scotland's controlled bowling kept the Afghans on a leash - Afghanistan were checked early, losing Gulbadin Naib and Sediqullah Atal inside the first four overs, and for a moment it felt like the pitch had a few questions to ask. It was on the slower side, yes, but still a surface where runs were there for the taking if you were patient. Darwish Rasooli and Ibrahim Zadran read it perfectly. They steadied the ship, took a cautious Powerplay to 41/2, and then slowly turned the dial up. A couple of timely big overs flipped the momentum, and their 82-run stand became the launchpad for what followed.

Afghanistan finish strongly - That's a solid comeback by Afghanistan in the second half of the innings. They were 77/2 at the end of the tenth over, and smashed 107 runs in the next sixty balls. Apart from Mark Watt and Brad Currie, there was little resistance as the scoring rate kept climbing. Seven of the last ten overs went into double figures, a telling stretch that underlined Scotland’s need to clamp down harder when the game drifts into the death.

Commentary.Commentary: All set to get underway in Bengaluru. Time to sharpen the rough edges. The Scottish players spread out to the field. Ibrahim Zadran and Gulbadin Naib are the two openers for Afghanistan. Brad Currie will bowl the first over. Naib to face. Here we go!

The captain of Scotland - Richie Berrington says that they are happy to bowl. Adds that it has been a good couple of days and they will give their best here. Adds that they are enjoying here and the facilities are great. Ends by saying that they are looking forward to taking on the challenge.

The captain of Afghanistan - Rashid Khan says that they will bat first. Mentions that they will look to put a good score on the board and get used to the conditions here. Adds that the preparation has been great and they got good practices. Ends by saying that they will give opportunities to everyone and improve on the spots where they are weak.

Scotland - Finlay McCreath, George Munsey, Michael Jones, Richie Berrington (C), Michael Leask, Tom Bruce, Matthew Cross (WK), Brandon McMullen, Brad Wheal, Brad Currie, Chris Greaves, Mark Watt, Oliver Davidson, Safyaan Sharif, Zainullah Ihsan.

Afghanistan - Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Azmatullah Omarzai, Gulbadin Naib, Mohammad Nabi, Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Shahidullah Kamal, Mohammad Ishaq, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Naveen-ul-Haq, Noor Ahmad, Rashid Khan (C), Fazalhaq Farooqi, Abdullah Ahmadzai.
TOSS - The coin flip lands in favor of Afghanistan and they have opted to BAT first.

Chance opened, belief followed - Scotland, meanwhile, rely heavily on their aggressive top order and their impressive group of all-rounders to stay competitive. George Munsey and Michael Jones will be vital in setting the tone, with Brandon McMullen and skipper Richie Berrington anchoring the middle while also providing the firepower to accelerate. Their bowling strength lies in control rather than raw pace, with Mark Watt and Chris Greaves looking to squeeze in the middle overs, and Safyaan Sharif and Bradley Wheal tasked with striking early and at the death. If Scotland are to challenge Afghanistan here, they will need to be sharp in all three departments against a side that rarely gives anything away. Do stay tuned for the toss.

Courageous challengers - Afghanistan come in with one of the most complete squads in the tournament, built around elite spin and a deep, flexible batting unit. Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz provide the perfect blend of stability and explosiveness at the top, while Sediqullah Atal and Darwish Rasooli give the middle order composure, allowing Mohammad Nabi, Gulbadin Naib and Azmatullah Omarzai to control the tempo and finish strongly. With the ball, Rashid Khan, Noor Ahmad and Mujeeb Ur Rahman form a spin attack that can dominate any surface, backed by the swing and variations of Fazalhaq Farooqi and Naveen Ul Haq, making Afghanistan extremely hard to score against through all phases of the innings.

And so it begins - Warm-ups are where reputations are tested before the points are on the line. This clash between Afghanistan and Scotland is exactly that, a chance for both sides to measure themselves against contrasting styles and sharpen their plans ahead of the ICC T20 World Cup 2026. Hello and welcome to our coverage of the first warm-up game from the BCCI Centre of Excellence 1, Bengaluru.
